title: Hamburger on Wheat Bun with Large Patty

content.title: About
content.content: A hamburger is a classic fast‑food item consisting of a large beef patty (about 170 g) placed between a split wheat bun. It is often served with lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles, cheese, and various sauces.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first hamburger was served in the United States in the late 19th century.
A wheat bun gives a soft texture and a mild grain flavor compared with rye buns.
A 170 g patty is considered a “premium‑size” and is common in upscale fast‑food chains.
The hamburger has become an icon of American culture and is popular worldwide.
There are over 300 variations of toppings and sauces, ranging from classic to exotic.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The beef patty provides high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Red meat contains heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Hamburgers supply vitamins B12, B6, and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Complex carbohydrates
items.content: The wheat bun offers complex carbs that provide sustained energy.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: If made with whole‑grain flour, the bun adds fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: A large patty and bun make the hamburger calorie‑dense; moderation is key for weight management.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Beef contains saturated fats, which can affect cholesterol levels when consumed in excess.

items.title: Salt and sauces
items.content: Sauces often add significant sodium and sugar, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The wheat bun contains gluten, unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hamburgers are typically eaten by hand, holding the bun so the patty and toppings stay in place. Add fresh vegetables, cheese, avocado, or swap heavy sauces for lighter options.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store a prepared hamburger in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. For longer storage, separate the bun and patty, wrap each in airtight containers, and reheat the patty to an internal temperature of 71 °C before serving.
